holidays.name: National Banana Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in the creamy, custardy goodness of banana cream pie, topped with whipped cream and sliced bananas in a flaky crust. Bakers and pie lovers celebrate by baking, buying, or just face-planting into a slice.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it emerged from food-celebration calendars and pie enthusiasts. The dessert itself grew popular in the early 20th century as bananas became cheap and widely available in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Bananas became a mass-market fruit in the US in the late 1800s thanks to refrigerated shipping, which paved the way for banana-based desserts like banana cream pie and bananas Foster.

holidays.name: Read Across America Day
holidays.description: A nationwide celebration of reading, with kids and adults dressing up as storybook characters and reading aloud. It is timed to the birthday of Dr. Seuss, so expect lots of striped hats and green eggs and ham.
holidays.origin: Launched by the National Education Association in 1998 to motivate children to read. It was set on March 2 to honor Theodor Seuss Geisel, who was born on this date in 1904.
holidays.funFact: Dr. Seuss wrote Green Eggs and Ham after a bet with his publisher that he could write a book using only 50 different words. He won the bet.

holidays.name: Old Stuff Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to digging out, dusting off, and appreciating your old stuff instead of buying new things. Attics, basements, and junk drawers become treasure troves of forgotten memories, questionable fashion, and ancient cables.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance created to encourage people to rediscover and either enjoy, repurpose, or responsibly pass along items they already own.
holidays.funFact: Studies on decluttering suggest that people often feel strong emotional attachment to objects they have owned for years, a phenomenon related to the endowment effect, where we value things more simply because they are ours.

holidays.name: Peanut Butter Lover's Day
holidays.description: A sticky, nutty celebration for fans of the beloved spread. Enthusiasts mark the day with sandwiches, cookies, and spoonfuls straight from the jar, while trying not to talk for the next several minutes.
holidays.origin: Part of March's National Peanut Month, which was established in 1974 by a presidential proclamation to honor the peanut industry. Peanut butter fans later adopted this date for a day of spread-centered devotion.
holidays.funFact: It takes about 540 peanuts to make a single 12-ounce jar of peanut butter, and by law in the US, anything labeled peanut butter must contain at least 90 percent peanuts.

holidays.name: Texas Independence Day
holidays.description: Texans celebrate the state's declaration of independence from Mexico with parades, barbecues, and a lot of bluebonnets and lone-star pride. It is a state holiday with serious Lone Star swagger.
holidays.origin: On March 2, 1836, delegates at Washington-on-the-Brazos signed the Texas Declaration of Independence, establishing the Republic of Texas, which existed as an independent nation until it joined the United States in 1845.
holidays.funFact: The Texas Declaration of Independence was drafted in about a day and signed by 59 delegates, and the Republic of Texas had its own president, currency, and navy.
